clue.text: Country once believed to be somehow loaded with gold

indicators.note: loaded with means filled with, so the gold is placed inside the rearranged letters
somehow says the letters of the word loaded are put together in some other way

parts.note: OR is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A legendary land rumoured to be stuffed with gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges LOADED into ELDADO, and 'with' puts OR inside it after ELD.
explanation.definitionFit: The fabled South American land of riches that explorers once believed existed.

clue.text: Where a film may be kept away from the public

definitions.text: Where a film may be kept

explanation.surface: Somewhere a reel of film is stored out of sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Film sits inside a camera; the legal phrase describes a hearing held in private.

clue.text: If I'm a Gentile I'll eat my hat!

definitions.text: If I'm a Gentile I'll eat my hat!

parts.words: If I'm a Gentile I'll eat my hat!
parts.note: a hat named after a meat pastry; a non-Jew may eat pork, so eating the hat is no hardship for a Gentile

explanation.surface: Someone swearing they are not a Gentile, staking their headgear on it.
explanation.walkthrough: The hat is a flat-crowned style named after a British meat pastry; pork is not kosher, so only a Gentile could happily eat it.
explanation.definitionFit: A low, flat-topped hat style, also a British pork pastry that only a non-Jew would eat.

clue.text: Calculating snakes in the grass

explanation.surface: Scheming traitors are like serpents hiding in the lawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Calculating machines that sum figures; also venomous vipers lurking in long grass.

clue.text: Tear away with the proceeds of the fraud

explanation.surface: A thief snatching the loot from a swindle and fleeing.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull something loose by tearing; also a swindle or overpriced con, and what it brings in.

clue.text: Everyone enjoying themselves sooner or later

explanation.surface: A promise that the whole party will have fun eventually.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as everybody inside a jolly time, and as an idiom meaning eventually, when the moment is right.

clue.text: Can Spain's head resolve the problems of old age?

indicators.note: resolve is taken as breaking down and resetting the letters of the three words before it

explanation.surface: Whether the Spanish leader can sort out the woes of the elderly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resolve' rearranges CAN SPAINS HEAD; the possessive 's of Spain's counts its S here.
explanation.definitionFit: Assorted bodily soreness, typical complaints of the elderly.

clue.text: It's a shocking form of execution

definitions.text: It's a shocking form of execution

parts.words: It's a shocking form of execution
parts.note: shocking is literal: the punishment is death by a jolt of current

explanation.surface: A remark about a horrifying method of capital punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: The seat used in some US states to kill condemned prisoners by current.

clue.text: Which Roman interior reveals such colourful intensity?

indicators.note: interior says the letters sit inside the run of words Which Roman

explanation.surface: Asking which Roman's inner self shows such vivid passion.
explanation.definitionFit: The saturation or purity of a colour, its vividness.

clue.text: Don't shut up if eager to accommodate John Paul

indicators.note: to accommodate means to house, so one word holds the other within it

parts.note: eager means keen
John Paul was the name of two popes

explanation.surface: Advice to keep talking if keen to welcome a man called John Paul.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to accommodate' puts POPE inside KEEN. John Paul is the papal name of John Paul I and II.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave a shop or door unclosed is not to close it up.

clue.text: It directs a politician to go outside

indicators.note: to go outside tells the politician to wrap around the letter a

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Something instructing a politician to step out of doors.
explanation.definitionFit: A chart that shows the way and so guides a traveller.

clue.text: Communist country provides land for the gentry

parts.note: E for East, as in the Communist Eastern bloc
a country is a state

explanation.surface: A Communist nation hands land over to the upper classes.
explanation.walkthrough: Communist stands for East, as in the old Eastern bloc, abbreviated E.
explanation.definitionFit: A large country property with grounds, owned by landed families.

clue.text: Faint? Yes but otherwise out of danger

indicators.note: otherwise means the letters of the words Faint and Yes appear in another order

explanation.surface: A patient nearly passing out, yet happily safe.
explanation.definitionFit: Secure, protected from harm.

clue.text: She is a lawyer in the States

parts.note: DA is a District Attorney, a US public prosecutor

explanation.surface: A remark that a woman practises law in America.
explanation.walkthrough: A DA, District Attorney, is a US state prosecutor.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's first name, so a female person.

clue.text: Certainly not to be found along any street

definitions.text: Certainly not to be found along any street

parts.words: Certainly not to be found along any street
parts.note: an emphatic refusal, read literally as being on no road at all

explanation.surface: Something that cannot be seen on any road anywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: An emphatic phrase meaning not at all; a way is also a road.

clue.text: Which person is from the World Health Organisation?

explanation.surface: Asking which member of staff comes from the UN health agency.
explanation.definitionFit: The interrogative asking about a person; also the initials of the UN health body.

clue.text: Cockney says Show me the leather'!

indicators.note: a Cockney accent of East London would say the phrase show me with a sound near sham-wah

parts.note: the phrase as a Londoner says it

explanation.surface: A Londoner demanding to see the leather goods.
explanation.walkthrough: A Cockney is a working-class East Londoner; their pronunciation of 'show me' is taken to run close to the leather's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft goatskin or sheepskin leather used for polishing.

clue.text: Sir Alec's verbal humour is unsophisticated

parts.note: Sir Alec Douglas-Home, British Prime Minister 1963-64, gives his surname with the possessive
wordplay humour is a pun

explanation.surface: A claim that a famous politician's wordplay is crude and plain.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Alec Douglas-Home was a British Prime Minister in the 1960s.
explanation.definitionFit: Simple and plain, as if woven at home rather than refined.

clue.text: Tell against consumption of millet-just the opposite we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the phrase is taken by its sound

parts.note: eating millet with the order flipped gives millet then ate

explanation.surface: Arguing against eating grain, or rather its reverse, as reported.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ate millet' turned round is 'millet ate', which said aloud matches the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To work or count against an outcome, as evidence can.

clue.text: Solid body of men found by Henry Alan in the post exchange!

indicators.note: in puts the first pieces inside the shop's initials

parts.note: PX is a post exchange, a US military shop
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tight group of soldiers spotted by two men in a forces store.
explanation.walkthrough: PX is a US forces shop; 'in' puts H plus ALAN inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A close formation of troops, as in ancient Greek infantry.

clue.text: The way to give approval to a man of honour

parts.note: appro is short for approval, as in goods on appro
CH is a Companion of Honour

explanation.surface: How to bestow praise on a distinguished honoured person.
explanation.walkthrough: Goods 'on appro' are on approval; CH is Companion of Honour, a British order.
explanation.definitionFit: A road or route leading toward a place.

clue.text: Take back summary

explanation.surface: Retracting a short outline.
explanation.definitionFit: To take up again or reoccupy; also a brief recap or CV.

clue.text: British leader dismissed from barrack for making liquor

indicators.note: dismissed from says that letter is sent out of the word barrack
leader means the opening letter of British

explanation.surface: A British officer thrown out of army quarters for distilling spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' picks B from British, and 'dismissed from' removes it from BARRACK.
explanation.definitionFit: An Asian spirit distilled from rice or palm sap.

clue.text: Married Miss Liddell out of spite

parts.note: Alice Liddell inspired Lewis Carroll's Alice in Wonderland

explanation.surface: Someone wed Miss Liddell purely out of ill will.
explanation.walkthrough: Alice Liddell was the girl who inspired Lewis Carroll's Alice.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill will, a desire to harm.

clue.text: Bitter trouble from the sound of it

indicators.note: from the sound of it says the word is matched by how it is pronounced

parts.note: to trouble someone is to ail them

explanation.surface: Resentment brewing into strife, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: Bitter is a British type of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Bitter is a hoppy British beer, one kind of this brew.

clue.text: Listen Mr Twist, to his ballads

definitions.text: Listen Mr Twist, to his ballads

indicators.note: Twist, posing as Oliver's surname, tells us to twist the letters of Listen Mr

explanation.surface: Someone urging a Mr Twist to hear the songs of a wandering singer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twist' looks like the name of Dickens's Oliver Twist but rearranges LISTENMR.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval singer and poet who performed ballads.

clue.text: Old Persian viceroy needs South African gin

parts.note: SA is the abbreviation for South Africa
a gin is a snare or trap

explanation.surface: An ancient governor demanding a South African spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gin' is not the drink but a snare.
explanation.definitionFit: A provincial governor in the ancient Persian empire.

clue.text: Quarter of the bus crew doesn't work when it's cold

definitions.text: Quarter of the bus crew doesn't work when it's cold

parts.words: Quarter of the bus crew doesn't work when it's cold
parts.note: a bus crew is a driver and a ticket collector, so half the collector is a quarter of the crew; such a material conducts poorly at low temperature

explanation.surface: A grumble that one of the bus staff skives in cold weather.
explanation.walkthrough: Old British buses had a driver and a conductor; half a conductor is a quarter of the crew.
explanation.definitionFit: A material such as silicon whose conductivity rises with temperature.
